## Prague transport fragment, Ukrainian provisions priority and disarmament orders

**Sources on this page:** p209 A1, p209 B1, p209 B2, p209 C1, p209 C2. [Concise case study](../military/transport_and_disarmament_orders.md).

<a id="edition-cases-military-transport-and-disarmament-orders-prague-transport-fragment-ukrainian-provisions-priority-and-disarmament-orders"></a>



**Source edition and exact repair accounting: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026).** Published Nov19–21 key: Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier unreviewed machine candidates for p209 are preserved and credited; this is not a universal first-decipherment claim.

Childs p209 contains five physical parts from three telegrams intercepted on 19 November 1918. Hand transcription restores rows missed by OCR in A1 and B1, making their native source frames readable. B and C each have both numbered parts; only A's first part appears here.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transport-and-disarmament-orders-source-and-exact-costs"></a>

### Source and exact costs

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p209, PDF p212. The source crops preserve all five parts, their shared headers and the eight printed dashes in A1. Each counted length agrees with its printed RICHI label. No received coordinate is inserted, deleted, excluded or moved.

| Record | Source slots | Raw fixed → edited fixed | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Printed-dash fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p209 A1 | 224 | 104/112 → 112/112 | 0 | 8 |
| p209 B1 | 310 | 155/155 → 155/155 | 4 | 0 |
| p209 B2 | 230 | 115/115 → 115/115 | 3 | 0 |
| p209 C1 | 242 | 121/121 → 121/121 | 4 | 0 |
| p209 C2 | 182 | 91/91 → 91/91 | 4 | 0 |
| **Total** | **1,188** | **586/594 → 594/594** | **15** | **8** |

The 1,188 source slots comprise 1,180 valid ADFGVX coordinates and eight printed dashes.

“Fixed” describes output under the published square labels. It does not independently authenticate reference numbers, remove transmission mistakes or establish uniquely correct wording. Source-directed repairs remain proposals with their exact coordinate cost.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transport-and-disarmament-orders-a1-an-incomplete-statement-from-prague"></a>

### A1: an incomplete statement from Prague

The header reads `ZO'N v LP`, intercept `06.30 p.m., November19th`, followed by `22.35 (19/11) 2 TLE`; the delivered text is explicitly `1 TL`. It addresses `OK MACKENSEN` and reports that the Minister-President in Prague has made a statement concerning transport of Mackensen's army group on the Teschen route. The clause stops at Teschen, so the operative continuation is unknown. No permission, refusal, destination beyond Teschen or later transport decision is supplied.

Eight printed dashes occupy source indices 97–104. Filling them supplies the missing letters in `MACKENSEN`, `MINISTERPRAESIDENT`, `HAT`, `ERKLAERT`, `STRECKE` and `TESCHEN`, without changing any observed coordinate. This is a lexical restoration from the surviving text, not an independent unseen prediction.

The conspicuous adjective `TS8HESCHICHE` stays unchanged. Its context suggests Czech, but the edition neither changes the 8 label to a letter nor normalizes the malformed spelling. The missing second part is outside this edition.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transport-and-disarmament-orders-b1b2-food-transport-takes-priority-over-raw-materials"></a>

### B1/B2: food transport takes priority over raw materials

The two parts share `IWE v LP`, intercept `07.31 p.m., November19th`, and `04.00 (19/11) 2 TLE`. The message addresses `HEERESGR X KIEW`. Because of difficulties with food supply and shortage of transport, it orders the utmost acceleration of dispatching all provisions acquired or available in Ukraine, giving them priority over raw materials of every kind.

The first forty printed coordinates of B1 were omitted by the earlier OCR stream. Restoring the actual first source row gives the native 310-coordinate frame and the coherent order. This is a correction to the machine transcription, not an insertion into the received source.

B1's four single-coordinate repairs are `TRANSPORTMITTEC→TRANSPORTMITTEL`, `AHBEFOERDERUNG→ABBEFOERDERUNG`, `UKRAING→UKRAINE` and `BESCHAFFTGN→BESCHAFFTEN`. Its `ABMMD` label and final `LEBENSMITTELM` remain untouched. In B2, three observed-coordinate changes produce `AUCHDER` and `ABBEFOERDERUNG` from raw `AUCQ6ER` and `ABBE9OERDERUNG`. These local word repairs do not assign Q, 6 or 9 new global square meanings.

The ending `NO X J0192SM X BEWEGE X BERLIN` remains exactly as the baseline labels yield it. No reference number or agency expansion is inferred.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transport-and-disarmament-orders-c1c2-arms-surrendered-in-warsaw"></a>

### C1/C2: arms surrendered in Warsaw

The two numbered parts share `KOW WAU v LP`, intercept `08.05 p.m., November19th`, and `22.30 (19/11) 2 TLE`. The text says that a large number of organized units in the former General Government of Warsaw had given weapons to the Poles. It continues that there must be no doubt that it is dishonourable for organized units to allow themselves to be disarmed without a fight. This is the message's statement and instruction.

C1 needs four single-coordinate repairs: `GROSSEDNZAHL→GROSSEANZAHL`, two letters in `GESCCLOJSENER→GESCHLOSSENER`, and `ESDDRF→ESDARF`. The grammatical anomaly `HABENGROSSEANZAHL` is retained. Its first-row final group is visibly `GFXAF`: the two unknown slots in an earlier OCR candidate were fictitious, and no source-mask fills are counted here.

C2 has four single-coordinate repairs: `WESN→WENN`, `GESCHLOSNENE→GESCHLOSSENE`, `SICL→SICH` and `LNSSEN→LASSEN`. Its final `OHL X RMJAJJ970 GEH X OP` remains unnormalized. No J or numeral relabel is proposed.

### Evidence and reproduction

The [inputs](../../experiments/transport_and_disarmament_orders/inputs.json) preserve all literal source rows, headers, published key values and crop-rendering metadata. The [certificates](../../experiments/transport_and_disarmament_orders/certificates.json) enumerate all fifteen substitutions, eight fills and every plaintext pair's original source coordinates. The [prior candidate snapshot](../../experiments/transport_and_disarmament_orders/prior_candidates.json) retains the old OCR candidates, including readable B2/C bodies and frozen retrieval entries; the bounded publication check is not a universal priority claim.

The package [README](../../experiments/transport_and_disarmament_orders/README.md) gives reproduction commands. Its verifier compares an independent physical-column inverse with the project decoder, checks every repair against the literal source and confirms exact re-encryption under the unchanged square. Optional PDF verification authenticates the pinned full scan and all crop pixels. A source-compatible proposal does not prove unique historical wording, and the raw label inventory remains available for later independently supported interpretation.
